name: Envy (invidia) as capital vice
plainSummary: In this tradition, envy is sorrow or resentment at another's good—wishing to lower them or possess what is theirs in a disordered way.
description: Derived principle: invidia (envy) is the capital vice of sadness at another's excellence or happiness, distinct from righteous indignation at injustice; it tends toward detraction, schadenfreude, and hostility.
foundationStrengthRationale: Clear parallel with envy as analyzed in philosophy and psychology; theological packaging adds metaphysical claims not all accept.

pros.claim: Captures a stable psychological pattern—resentment of comparative status—that corrodes communities.
pros.evidence: Social science and virtue ethics both study status competition and envy-driven behavior.

cons.claim: Can blur into legitimate desire for fairness or anger at undeserved privilege.
cons.evidence: Distinguishing envy from warranted protest against inequality requires careful moral analysis.
